land.text: the enclave in Rome that the Lateran Treaty 'recognised as an independent state under the sovereignty of the Holy See'

predecessors.note: Rome was 'occupied and annexed in 1870' and ended the Papal States (Lateran Treaty page); Cliopatria's Kingdom of Italy row runs 587-1946 and is to be split by eu-13.

correction.text: Vatican City, 0.49 km2 in the infobox (44 hectares, 0.44 km2, in the lead)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The two area figures on the page differ (0.44 and 0.49 km2; the infobox follows a 1945-46 atlas correction); the state is a fraction of one grid cell (about 253 km2), so the renderer should draw a point. The Papal Palace of Castel Gandolfo and the major basilicas in Italy have extraterritorial status and are not territory.

region.text: Vatican City, the enclave in Rome

ledger.note: 11 February 1929: the Lateran Treaty creates Vatican City. The Lateran Treaty, 'signed on 11 February 1929' and ratified by the Italian Parliament on 7 June 1929, 'recognised Vatican City as an independent state under the sovereignty of the Holy See' and ended the Roman Question. The Vatican City page says it took effect on 7 June 1929, the month used here.

certainty.note: Fixed by the 1929 treaty; the German occupation of Rome after the September 1943 armistice and its liberation in 1944 respected Vatican City's neutral status (Vatican City page).

notes: A micro-state Cliopatria lacks (its Papal States row ends 1870). The end year 2026 is the project's last year, not an end. The Holy See, a sovereign entity distinct from the state, is not given a dossier. Not on the pages: the ruler list (popes; the page names Pope Leo XIV elected 8 May 2025), the Castel Gandolfo area.
